Dulcamara Bittersüss; Bittersweet; Douce-Amère; Dulcamarae Caulis; Woody Nightshade. Profile Dulcamara consists of the dried stems and branches of Solanum dulcamara (Solanaceae). It was formerly a popular remedy for chronic rheumatism and skin eruptions and was given as an infu- sion. All parts of the plant are poisonous due to the presence of solana- ceous alkaloids. The berries have caused poisoning in children. Adverse effects are treated as described under Atropine, p.1220. Homoeopathy. Dulcamara has been used in homoeopathic medicines under the following names: Solanum dulcamara; Dulc. Preparations Proprietary Preparations (details are given in Part 3) Ger.: Cefabene; Solapsor†.
